card.statement:
The class of morphisms satisfying <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.H>> <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.H-0>> - <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.H-3>> is weakly stable. We denote this class of morphisms by $\mathrm{HR}$, standing for ``horizontally right adjointable". Similarly, we let $\mathrm{HL}$ denote the class of morphisms satisfying <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.HL>> <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.HL-0>>-<<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.H-6>>, let $\mathrm{VR}$ denote the class of morphisms satisfying <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.V>> <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.V-0>>-<<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.V-3>>, and let $\mathrm{VL}$ denote the class of morphisms satisfying <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.VL>> <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.VL-0>>-<<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.V-6>>.

- Suppose $\bfC_\horiz= \bfC$ (so every object is as in <<ref:ex:commutative-algebra-in-corr(C)>>). Then giving <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.H>> <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.H-2>>, <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.H>> <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.H-3>> is equivalent to the projection formula

\[
f\horizr(\mF)\otimes \mG\cong f\horizr(\mF\otimes f\horizl(\mG)),\quad \mbox{for }\ \mF\in \der(X), \ \mG\in \der(Y).
\]

Indeed, by letting $Z=Y$ applying $(\Delta_Y)\horizl$ to <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.H>> <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.H-3>> gives the projection formula. Conversely, Let $p_X: X\times Z\to X, q_Y: Y\times Z\to Y$ and $p_Z: X\times Z\to Z, q_Z: Y\times Z\to Z$ be the projections. Then

\begin{eqnarray*}
f\horizr\mF\boxtimes_{\La}\mG&=&(q_Y)\horizl(f\horizr\mF)\otimes (q_Z)\horizl\mG\cong (f\times \id)\horizr ((p_X)\horizl\mF) \otimes (q_Z)\horizl\mG \\
&\cong& (f\times\id)\horizr( (p_X)\horizl\mF) \otimes (p_Z)\horizl\mG)=(f\times\id)(\mF\boxtimes_{\La}\mG).
\end{eqnarray*}

Similar remarks apply to other situations. E.g. giving <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.V>> <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.V-2>>, then <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.V>> <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.V-3>> is equivalent to $f\vertr(\mF\otimes\mG)\cong f\vertr\mF\otimes f\horizl\mG$ for $\mF\in \der(Y)$ and $\mG\in\der(Z)$.

- Sometimes the sheaf theory $\shv$ satisfies even stronger assumptions. E.g. it may happen that for some $f\in \mathrm{HL}$, there is a natural isomorphism $(f\horizl)^L\cong f\vertl$ such that the base change isomorphisms and projection formula for $(f\horizl)^L$ as from <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.H-4>>-<<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.H-6>> are equivalent to the corresponding base change isomorphisms and projection formula for $f\vertl$ as encoded in the sheaf theory. See <<ref:prop-sheaf-theory-for-adjoint-factorization>>. The same remark applies to other cases considered in <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.H>> <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.V>> and <<ref:assumptions.base.change.sheaf.theory.VL>>.

paper.title: Tame categorical local Langlands correspondence
paper.abstract: In one of our previous articles, we outlined the formulation of a version of the categorical arithmetic local Langlands conjecture. The aims of this article are threefold. First, we provide a detailed account of one component of this conjecture: the local Langlands category. Second, we aim to prove this conjecture in the tame case for quasi-split unramified reductive groups. Finally, we will explore the first applications of such categorical equivalence.
